text:
mike: Hey team — found partner webhook logs that include presigned S3 URLs in plaintext. Looks like they were pasted in a partner's debugging output and shipped to their logging pipeline.
elaine: Ugh. How many URLs / timeframe?
mike: ~120 URLs across 3 days (2026-03-18 to 2026-03-20). Most are PUT presigned urls to our uploads bucket.
priya: Do the URLs directly grant object write/read access or are they tied to short-lived creds?
mike: They are pre-signed S3 object URLs (expires in 7d originally). The query params contain X-Amz-Signature and key info.
samir: Presigned URLs can't be revoked per-object. If the URL is leaked you either wait for expiry or remove the object / rotate the underlying signing key.
priya: Right — options: 1) If objects already created, we can delete them; 2) shorten expiry going forward; 3) rotate the KMS key used to generate signatures if we use a signing service that depends on a key; 4) rotate service credentials that issue presigned URLs.
mike: For scope: of the 120 urls, 82 were used to upload objects (we can see PUTs), 38 were unused. Some point to partner-specific prefixes.
elaine: Immediate action: take down objects created by leaked URLs (if sensitive) and revoke any IAM creds that allowed presign generation.
priya: I'll handle the IAM/service-account rotation for the presign generator. Which SA is it?
mike: It's svc-upload-generator@redwood. I can trigger a revoke/rotation but need owner sign-off for breaking active uploads.
ops-oncall: We should create an incident ticket and set priority. If uploaded objects are non-sensitive, maybe low-sev, but can't assume.
sec-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1039. Incident channel: #inc-3135799999 (automated).
samir: Quick containment checklist:
- Identify objects uploaded via those PUTs (mike has list)
- Snapshot object metadata (don't delete until snapshot unless sensitive)
- Delete objects confirmed sensitive
- Rotate generator SA keys (priya)
- Rotate any KMS keys / rewrap objects if they were encrypted
- Shorten presign TTL in service config to 30s for hotfix
- Add logging filters to drop presigned URLs from partner payloads
priya: For KMS: our standard flow is to create a new key, re-encrypt objects with the new CMK, then retire old key. If objects are already public via URL usage, deleting is simpler.
mike: I'm pasting the small list of affected keys (obfuscated here):
```
uploads/partnerA/2026/03/18/obj-abc123
uploads/partnerA/2026/03/19/obj-def456
uploads/partnerB/2026/03/20/obj-ghi789
```
elaine: Mike, mark which of those are sensitive. If any contain PII, escalate to legal/compliance.
mike: obj-abc123 contains user PII — will mark as sensitive. obj-def456 is image asset, low sensitivity. obj-ghi789 is partner metadata (non-PII).
priya: I'll rotate svc-upload-generator creds now. Steps I'll run:
- disable current key in Vault for svc-upload-generator
- create new key pair
- update presign service to use new creds (deploy)
- run smoke presign checks
- publish rollback plan
samir: For immediate cleanup, run:
```
aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-uploads --key "uploads/partnerA/2026/03/18/obj-abc123"
aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-uploads --key "uploads/partnerA/2026/03/19/obj-def456"
aws s3api delete-object --bucket redwood-uploads --key "uploads/partnerB/2026/03/20/obj-ghi789"
```
mike: I'll take the delete for the PII object after snapshotting metadata to S3: `s3 cp s3://redwood-uploads/uploads/partnerA/2026/03/18/obj-abc123 s3://redwood-incident-backups/3135799999/` then delete.
ops-oncall: Please post runbook snippet for rotation and ETA. We'll page infra if any deploys are required.
priya: Runbook snippet:
1) Vault: create new secret at secret/data/svc-upload-generator
2) Update presign service env var PRESIGN_KEY=... and deploy to staging
3) Smoke test: attempt a presign + PUT + GET
4) Deploy to prod and monitor errors > 5% roll back
Estimated ETA: rotate creds and deploy in 45m.
elaine: I'll notify partner security contact and legal (FYI). Use caution in notifications — don't paste leaked URLs.
mike: Notifying partner now. pinging @partner-sec and copying incident ID.
sec-bot: PagerDuty alert created for oncall escalation (pd-INC-2026-1039).
samir: After creds rotated, we should run a search in partner logs for any other embedded URLs or tokens and add a prevention rule at ingestion.
priya: Also adding a sanitizer to our webhook ingest lambda to scrub query params matching X-Amz- or authorization headers.
mike: I'll push a quick scrub patch to staging in 20m and to prod after validation.
elaine: Summary actions and owners:
- Delete PII object + backup: mike
- Delete non-sensitive objects: mike (after confirmation)
- Rotate svc-upload-generator creds: priya
- Shorten presign TTL and deploy config change: samir
- Notify partner/legal: elaine
- Create ingestion sanitizer: mike + priya
- Incident tracking: ops-oncall
mike: Thanks all. I'll update INC-2026-1039 with timestamps and deletion artifacts.
ops-oncall: Keep this thread updated. If anything blocks deploy, ping me and I'll escalate.
priya: Rotation started (disabling old Vault secret) — will post when new key is live.
mike: Deletion of obj-abc123 completed and snapshot uploaded to incident bucket (audit tag: INC-2026-1039).
